name: Romania

findings.local_actor: Romanian Government / CSAT; operators Vodafone, Orange, Telekom Romania, Digi
findings.reversal_of: Huawei (and likely ZTE) equipment in Romanian operators' mobile core and radio networks
findings.summary: Under Romania's June 2021 5G security law, only CSAT-cleared vendors may supply 5G gear; in early 2024 the government rejected Huawei's authorisation and its appeal, forcing removal from cores within five years and RAN within seven.
findings.analyst_inference: Coded as reversal of operational (tier 5) Huawei network equipment: Developing Telecoms (2021) reports Digi, Orange, Telekom Romania and Vodafone all used Huawei/ZTE alongside Nokia/Ericsson. Reason geopolitical (national-security assessment by CSAT). Huawei sued CSAT, the digitisation ministry and the PM in 2024; outcome not established in sources opened, so still_current null. A Romania-US 5G memorandum is mentioned by Romania Insider (2023) as context but was not separately coded because no dated primary source was opened.

findings.summary: Vodafone Romania, which per Strand Consult relied entirely on Chinese vendors for 4G RAN, is replacing Huawei with Ericsson on about 80% of urban sites and Samsung on about 20%; rural sites shared with Orange face a separate tender.
findings.analyst_inference: Ericsson (Sweden) and Samsung (Korea) are both third pole; combined in one finding because the split is a single replacement programme. Tier 3 assumes vendor awards were signed; no contract value or date found. Orange Romania's replacement vendor was not named in sources opened. Ericsson, Samsung and Nokia hold CSAT 5G authorisations (Romania Insider, Aug 2023), which is a regulatory clearance, not coded as adoption.

findings.summary: ClusterPower and equity partner AIC announced an 800MW AI data-centre region near Craiova: 512MW in three phases at Mischii (70MW ready end-2026) plus about 300MW at Fauresti from 2029; ClusterPower already operates a Mischii facility.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole domestic because ClusterPower was founded by Romanian entrepreneurs (DCD 2021); AIC's stake size and nationality were not stated, so control could shift. Tier 3 for a signed equity partnership with no disclosed value; the expansion's construction start was not confirmed. First Mischii phase launched April 2022 per DCD. Both sources are one host, so not corroborated. DCD describes the infrastructure as Nvidia-certified; no GPU deployment coded.

findings.controller: ICI Bucharest with Politehnica Bucharest, co-funded under EuroHPC JU
findings.local_actor: National Institute for Research and Development in Informatics (ICI Bucharest)
findings.summary: Romania was selected in October 2025 for a EuroHPC AI Factory hosted by ICI Bucharest with Politehnica Bucharest, to acquire an AI-optimised supercomputer; the institute's director expected operation around spring 2027.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole null: hosted by a Romanian state institute but EuroHPC AI Factory systems are typically co-owned by the EU joint undertaking, so control sits between domestic and third (EU); ownership split not found. Tier 2 because selection/project start only, no procurement award seen. Budget and accelerator vendor not stated in any source opened; no silicon finding coded.

findings.controller: OpenLLM-Ro (Politehnica Bucharest, University of Bucharest, Institute for Logic and Data Science)
findings.local_actor: OpenLLM-Ro research consortium (funded by BRD Groupe Societe Generale)
findings.summary: Romanian researchers released OpenLLM-Ro, open-weight Romanian-language models (RoLlama2-7b, RoMistral-7b) fine-tuned from Llama 2 and Mistral, with datasets and code on Hugging Face; no government deployment is described.
findings.analyst_inference: Weights released by Romanian academic bodies, so domestic; academic rather than state-run, and scale 'national' only as the reference Romanian-language model. Main base is Llama 2 (Meta, us); RoMistral's base is Mistral (EU, third). Search results show a later RoLlama3.1-8b, not opened. Tier 2: research release, no adoption found. BRD is a Societe Generale subsidiary (funder only).

findings.local_actor: Romanian public bodies incl. at least 28 army units, SRI, county police, Border Police, Gendarmerie, prisons, Senate
findings.summary: RFE/RL found Hikvision or Dahua cameras bought through public procurement by hundreds of Romanian institutions, including military units at Deveselu and Cyber Defence Command; no ban exists, and about 200,000 such devices were internet-connected in 2021.

sources.publisher: Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty Romania (Europa Libera)

findings.analyst_inference: Coded as tier 5 (widely operational) but these are mostly small direct purchases, not an integrated safe-city system. RFE/RL is US-government funded, so coded S4 under the state-affiliated rule even though it is investigative reporting citing procurement records; reviewer may reclassify. Defence ministry says its systems are closed-circuit.

silicon.null_reason: no named accelerator purchase found; AI Factory hardware vendor and ClusterPower GPU deployments not disclosed in sources opened

power.null_reason: no AI-specific plant surfaced beyond ClusterPower's onsite gas generation and substation, recorded in ROU-003

research_gaps: Status of Huawei's lawsuit against CSAT/government over the 2024 5G authorisation denial, including any Constitutional Court (CCR) referral and a court order to disclose classified documents (RFE/RL page could not be opened).
Date, text and current status of the Romania-US 5G security memorandum (reported as 2019).
Orange Romania, Telekom/Digi replacement vendors for Huawei RAN/core and progress against the 2026 core / 2028 RAN deadlines.
ZTE: was any authorisation request filed or denied?
EuroHPC RO AI Factory: budget, EU/national split, ownership of the system, and accelerator vendor once procured.
ClusterPower/AIC: AIC stake and domicile; whether MSC1 70MW phase construction has started; tenants and GPU vendor.
Any Romanian government adoption of a frontier model provider (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Mistral) or a state-backed national LLM.
Whether any Romanian authority has acted to restrict Hikvision/Dahua cameras since February 2024.
